title: Safe Generator Use for Y2K: CPSC, DeVilbiss Air Power Company Alert Consumers About Gasoline Tanks on Certain Portable Generators
reason: CPSC and DAPC are investigating whether the fuel tanks on the generators can crack where the tanks mount on the frame, posing a fire hazard. As a precaution until that evaluation is complete, consumers should not put more than three gallons of gasoline in the fuel tanks at any time.
firm: DeVilbiss Air Power Company (DAPC), of Jackson, Tenn.
distribution: These generators were sold nationwide from February 1996 until June 1999.
hazards: CPSC and DAPC are investigating whether the fuel tanks on the generators can crack where the tanks mount on the frame, posing a fire hazard. As a precaution until that evaluation is complete, consumers should not put more than three gallons of gasoline in the fuel tanks at any time.
remedies: Any consumer who has seen leakage from the tank should not use the generator and should contact DAPC to obtain a free warranty replacement tank.
injuries: Each year, carbon monoxide from fuel-burning appliances kills approximately 200 people and sends 10,000 people to hospital emergency rooms. Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning are similar to the flu, including nausea, headache, dizziness, and irregular breathing. Exposure to high levels of carbon monoxide can cause death.

title: CPSC, Burger King Corporation Announce Voluntary Recall of Pokemon Ball
reason: The balls may pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age. Pokemon balls are the ball-shaped plastic containers that hold Pokemon toys in Burger King kids meals. Either half of the Pokemon ball can become stuck on a child's face, covering the nose and mouth and may cause suffocation of a child under three years of age.
distribution: Burger King restaurants nationwide distributed the Pokemon balls inside Burger King Kids Club Meals and regular kids meals from early November through December, 1999.
hazards: The balls may pose a suffocation hazard to children under three years of age. Pokemon balls are the ball-shaped plastic containers that hold Pokemon toys in Burger King kids meals. Either half of the Pokemon ball can become stuck on a child's face, covering the nose and mouth and may cause suffocation of a child under three years of age.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the balls away from children under the age of three. They should discard the ball or return both halves of the ball to a Burger King restaurant for a free small order of french fries. Consumers may continue to use the Pokemon toy that came inside the ball. Burger King restaurants will continue to distribute the Pokemon toys in balls with Burger King Big Kids Meals, but the Pokemon balls will no longer be included with the toy in the regular kids club meals, generally intended for younger children. Consumers should not allow younger children under the age of three to play with these balls.
injuries: A 13-month-old girl reportedly suffocated when one-half of a Pokemon ball covered her nose and mouth. An 18-month-old girl reportedly also had a ball-half stuck over her face, causing her distress. However, the girl's father (on the second attempt) pulled the ball-half from her face.

title: CPSC, Neiman Marcus Announce Recall of "CerArte" Candles
reason: The painted surfaces on these candles can ignite, spark, burn rapidly, and drip wax, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Neiman Marcus sold 22 different styles of "CerArte" candles through December 22, 1999. The candles sold for approximately $15 to $35. These same candles may have been sold at other retail stores.
hazards: The painted surfaces on these candles can ignite, spark, burn rapidly, and drip wax, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these candles immediately and return them to any Neiman Marcus store for a refund.
injuries: Neiman Marcus received several reports from consumers, including one where these candles sparked and burned so rapidly that hot wax spilled from the candle onto adjoining surfaces. No injuries were reported.

title: CPSC, Hanna's Candle Co. Announce Recall of Millennium Candles Sold at SAM'S CLUB Stores
reason: The candle holder can crack when the burning wick touches the side of the glass, causing lacerations.
firm: Hanna's Candle Co., of Fayetteville, Ark.
distribution: SAM'S CLUB stores nationwide sold these candles, from October 1999 through November 1999, for about $20.
hazards: The candle holder can crack when the burning wick touches the side of the glass, causing lacerations.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these candles immediately and return them to any SAM'S CLUB store for a full refund.
injuries: There have been two incidents of cracked glass but no injuries reported with this product.

title: CPSC, Rich Pacific Ltd. Announce Recall of Christmas Lights
product: Rich Pacific miniature Christmas lights and icicle-style lights
reason: CPSC has found that these lights have undersized wires, that can pull out of the plugs and individual light sockets, posing shock or fire hazards.
distribution: Pergament Home Center stores in New York sold these lights, from October 1999 through December 1999, for between $2 and $6.
hazards: CPSC has found that these lights have undersized wires, that can pull out of the plugs and individual light sockets, posing shock or fire hazards.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these lights and return them to the store where purchased, for store credit.
injuries: CPSC and Rich Pacific have not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these light sets.

title: CPSC, Kelty Announce Recall to Repair Backpack Child Carriers
reason: The seat height adjustment strap on these carriers can slip out of the buckle. A child can slide downward in the seat unexpectedly and could fall out of the carrier.
distribution: Specialty and sporting good retailers, including L.L. Bean, REI and Eastern Mountain Sports, sold the recalled backpack carriers nationwide, from March 1999 through December 1999, for between $100 and $250.
hazards: The seat height adjustment strap on these carriers can slip out of the buckle. A child can slide downward in the seat unexpectedly and could fall out of the carrier.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these backpack carriers, and contact Kelty for instructions on getting the free repair kit.
injuries: Kelty has received two reports of children slipping down inside the carriers after the height adjustment strap came loose. Neither child fell out of the carrier, and there were no reports of injury.

title: CPSC, Fashion Bug Announce Recall of Christmas Candles
product: Fashion Bug gold-colored candles (Christmas tree or cherubs)
reason: The gold coating on these candles can ignite, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Fashion Bug and Fashion Bug Plus stores nationwide sold the candles, from November 1999 through December 1999, for about $4.
hazards: The gold coating on these candles can ignite, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these candles immediately and return them to any Fashion Bug store, for a refund.
injuries: Fashion Bug received a report from a consumer, that the gold coating on one of these candles ignited. No injuries or property damage were reported.

title: CPSC, Safari Ltd. Announce Recall of Magnet Games
reason: Paint on the magnets metal figures contains amounts of lead that exceed federal standards for children's products. Prolonged exposure to high levels of lead presents a lead poisoning hazard to young children.
distribution: Small toy and gift stores nationwide sold these magnets, from January 1999 through November 1999, for about $6.
hazards: Paint on the magnets metal figures contains amounts of lead that exceed federal standards for children's products. Prolonged exposure to high levels of lead presents a lead poisoning hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately remove the metal figures from the magnetic base and discard them.
injuries: CPSC and Safari Ltd. are not aware of any injuries involving these products.

title: CPSC, NHTSA and Kolcraft Announce Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
reason: When used as an infant carrier, the handle can unexpectedly move from the intended carrying position, causing the seat to suddenly rotate. When this happens, the infant can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
distribution: Juvenile product, mass merchandise and major discount stores nationwide sold the car seat/carriers, beginning in January 1993, for about $30 to $60, when sold alone, or $100 to $150, when sold with strollers.
hazards: When used as an infant carrier, the handle can unexpectedly move from the intended carrying position, causing the seat to suddenly rotate. When this happens, the infant can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries.
remedies: Check the label on the side of the product for the manufacturing date and five-digit model/style number and contact Kolcraft, which will provide, free of charge, an easy-to-install repair kit. Until the carrier has been repaired, do not to carry the seat by its handle, but by the head and foot of the seat. The seat still can and should be used as a car seat.
injuries: There have been more than 3,000 reports of handle-related problems, the majority of which report that the handle of the infant car seat/carrier unexpectedly moved from the intended use position, resulting in 42 injuries to infants. Some children were restrained in the carrier and others were not. These injuries range from a skull fracture and concussions to cuts, scrapes and bruises.

title: CPSC, Jingle Bell Enterprises Inc. Announce Recall of Christmas Lights
product: Jingle Bell miniature Christmas lights and icicle-style lights
reason: These lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and individual light sockets, posing fire and shock hazards.
firm: Jingle Bell Enterprise Inc., of Philadelphia Pa.
distribution: Hardware and garden stores sold the light sets mainly in Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey and New York, from November 1999 through December 1999, for between $5 and $8.
hazards: These lights have undersized wires that can easily pull out of the plugs and individual light sockets, posing fire and shock hazards.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these lights, and return them to the store where purchased for either a refund or a replacement set of lights.
injuries: CPSC and Jingle Bell Enterprises have not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these light sets.

title: CPSC, Käthe Kruse Doll Co. Announce Recall of "Selecta" Wooden Toys
product: Selecta wooden toys: "Quatrino" wooden shape sorter toys, "Sorting Box" shape sorter toys, "Favola" shape sorter toys, and "Kugelbahn" ball chute toys
reason: The balls included with these toys are banned because they present a serious risk of choking deaths to young children.
distribution: Toy stores and websites sold these toys, from January 1997 through November 1999, for $30 to $80.
hazards: The balls included with these toys are banned because they present a serious risk of choking deaths to young children.
remedies: Consumers should take these toys away from young children immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund. Consumers who purchased the toys from a website should contact the website to make arrangements for returning the toys for a refund.
injuries: The CPSC and Käthe Kruse Doll Co. are not aware of any injuries involving the small balls contained in these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent possible injuries.

title: CPSC, Royce Union Bicycles Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Men's Mountain Bicycles
product: Royce Union ABT 2000 Mountain Bicycles (model no. 16368)
reason: The frames of these bikes can break apart, causing falls and serious injuries to riders.
firm: Royce Union Bicycles Co. Inc., of Hauppauge, N.Y.
distribution: Sears stores sold these bikes nationwide, from April 1998 through September 1999, for about $300.
hazards: The frames of these bikes can break apart, causing falls and serious injuries to riders.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop riding these bicycles, and call Royce Union for information on receiving a free replacement bicycle.
injuries: Royce Union has received four reports of the bicycle frames breaking resulting in serious head and back injuries, as well as abrasions and contusions to riders.

title: CPSC, Huffy Bicycle Co. Announce Recall of Men's Mountain Bicycles
product: Huffy ALX 1000 bicycles (model no. 26809); ALX 1500 bicycles (model no. 26849), and Aluminum 300 bicycles (model no. K6809)
reason: The frames of these bicycles can break apart, causing falls and serious injuries to riders.
firm: Huffy Bicycle Co., of Miamisburg, Ohio
distribution: Discount department stores and sporting good stores, including Kmart, Ames, The Sports Authority, Service Merchandise and TRU*SERV, sold these bicycles nationwide, from June 1998 through September 1999, for about $160.
hazards: The frames of these bicycles can break apart, causing falls and serious injuries to riders.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop riding these bicycles, and call Huffy for information on receiving a free replacement bicycle.
injuries: Huffy has received two reports of the bicycle frames breaking, resulting in serious head and back injuries, as well as abrasions and contusions to riders.

title: CPSC, Gap Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Pajamas
product: Children's pajamas sold at Gap and Old Navy stores
reason: The pajama sets fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards. The standards require sleepwear to be flame-resistant, and if the fabric ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burns to children.
firm: Gap Inc., of San Francisco, Calif.
distribution: GapKids, babyGap, Gap Outlet and Old Navy stores nationwide sold these pajamas, from August 1999 through December 1999, for between $20 and $39.
hazards: The pajama sets fail to meet federal children's sleepwear flammability standards. The standards require sleepwear to be flame-resistant, and if the fabric ignites, the flame must self-extinguish. Failure to meet the flammability standards presents a risk of serious burns to children.
remedies: Parents and caregivers should immediately stop allowing children to wear these pajamas and return them to any Gap or Old Navy location for a refund and a $10 gift certificate.
injuries: Gap Inc. has not received any reports of injuries related to these pajama sets.

title: CPSC, Viking Sewing Machines Recall Sewing Machines
reason: When removing the sewing machine's power cord from the power transformer on the sewing machine, loose pins from the power transformer could remain in the cord, posing a risk of electric shock.
firm: Viking Sewing Machines Inc., of Cleveland, Ohio
distribution: Authorized Viking dealers sold these sewing machines nationwide, from January 1998 through September 1998, for about $4,000.
hazards: When removing the sewing machine's power cord from the power transformer on the sewing machine, loose pins from the power transformer could remain in the cord, posing a risk of electric shock.
remedies: Consumers should only unplug these machines from the wall outlet, and should not remove the power cord from the sewing machine power transformer. Consumers should call an authorized Viking dealer to arrange for a free safety inspection. If needed, the dealer will replace the defective power transformer free of charge.

title: CPSC, Southern Exchange Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Camp Mess Kits
reason: The mess kit's sauce pan handle does not lock into place and the mess kit's fry pan handle can bend during use, spilling hot foods or liquids onto consumers and causing serious burns.
distribution: Camping, mass merchandise and army surplus stores nationwide and in Puerto Rico sold the mess kit, from May 1994 through September 1999, for about $3.
hazards: The mess kit's sauce pan handle does not lock into place and the mess kit's fry pan handle can bend during use, spilling hot foods or liquids onto consumers and causing serious burns.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the mess kit immediately and return it to the store where purchased, for a refund or replacement mess kit.
injuries: CPSC and Texsport have received one report of a 10-year-old boy who received second-degree burns to his ankle when boiling water spilled from the sauce pan he was using.

title: CPSC, Northern Bedroom's Inc. Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
reason: The top bunk does not have guardrails on both sides. A child could fall or become entrapped between the wall and the mattress if there are not guardrails on the top bunk.
firm: Northern Bedroom's Inc., of Oxford, Maine
distribution: Furniture and specialty bedroom stores throughout the New England states sold the beds, from May 1995 through February 1998, for about $300 to $550.
hazards: The top bunk does not have guardrails on both sides. A child could fall or become entrapped between the wall and the mattress if there are not guardrails on the top bunk.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled beds immediately and email the company to receive free guardrails for the top bunk.
injuries: CPSC is not aware of any deaths associated with the beds being recalled. However, since 1990, CPSC has received reports of seven children who died from becoming entrapped between the bed and the wall in upper bunks of bunk beds without guardrails.

title: CPSC, Sunbeam® Announce Recall of Glow-In-the-Dark Humidifiers
product: Sunbeam®, Hankscraft® and SunMark® humidifiers with water tanks that glow in the dark
reason: These humidifiers can develop an electrical short, presenting a fire hazard.
firm: Sunbeam Corp., of Boca Raton, Fla.
distribution: Discount department and drug stores sold these humidifiers nationwide, from March 1995 through December 1997, for $8 to $15.
hazards: These humidifiers can develop an electrical short, presenting a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these humidifiers, and call Sunbeam for instructions on returning the products for a free replacement.
injuries: Sunbeam has received 87 complaints from consumers using these humidifiers, including 42 reports of fire. Three consumers suffered smoke inhalation and another suffered minor burns to her hands.

title: CPSC, Manufacturers Announce Recall to Replace Toy and Youth Basketball Nets
reason: Children could strangle on loops or openings in nets that come unhooked from the rim or have knots that slide. If children put their heads into these openings, the net can get tangled around their necks.
firm: Franklin Sports, of Stoughton, Mass.; Huffy Sports, of Sussex, Wis.; Lifetime Products, of Clearfield, Utah
distribution: Toy, sporting goods, mass merchandise and discount department stores nationwide sold the basketball sets since 1993, for $13 to $40.
hazards: Children could strangle on loops or openings in nets that come unhooked from the rim or have knots that slide. If children put their heads into these openings, the net can get tangled around their necks.
remedies: Consumers should remove and throw away nets that can unhook or have knots that slide. Manufacturers will send consumers new nets that securely attach to the rim and do not have sliding knots. The basketball set can be used without a net until the new net arrives. Consumers should not return the product to stores.
injuries: Franklin Sports has received one report of a 3-year-old boy getting his head and neck caught in a basketball net. Huffy Sports and Lifetime Products have received no incident reports. No injuries have been reported. In December 1998, Fisher Price, Little Tikes, Ohio Art and Today's Kids recalled 10.1 million toy basketball sets to replace their nets. This recall followed 20 reports of children under 5 getting their heads and necks caught in the nets, including the death of an 18-month-old child.

title: CPSC, JumpSport Recalls Trampoline Safety Net Enclosures
reason: The straps on the bottom of the net can break. Children can fall out under the net and off the trampoline and be injured.
firm: Trampoline Safety Net Enclosures Inc., of Saratoga, Calif.
distribution: Costco, BJ's, Academy and Bradlees stores nationwide sold the safety nets, from February 1999 to July 1999, for about $150 to $230.
hazards: The straps on the bottom of the net can break. Children can fall out under the net and off the trampoline and be injured.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the safety nets immediately and contact JumpSport. JumpSport will send consumers free replacement bottom straps.
injuries: JumpSport has received two reports of children falling off the trampoline when the straps on the bottom of the enclosure broke. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, J.C. Penney Announce Recall of Boys Jackets
reason: There are 7-inch drawstrings at the bottom of the jackets. Children could be dragged if the drawstrings catch in a vehicle's door, and suffer injury or death.
firm: J.C. Penney Co. Inc., of Plano, Texas
distribution: J.C. Penney stores nationwide sold the jackets, from June 1999 to November 1999, for about $30.
hazards: There are 7-inch drawstrings at the bottom of the jackets. Children could be dragged if the drawstrings catch in a vehicle's door, and suffer injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the jackets immediately. Either remove the drawstrings or return the jacket to the nearest J.C. Penney store for a full refund.
injuries: J.C. Penney is not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these jackets. Since 1991, CPSC knows of 6 deaths and 8 injuries to children from coat drawstrings catching in bus or car doors.

title: CPSC & Sea & Sea Underwater Photography Recall Underwater Strobes
product: Underwater camera strobe light, model number YS-50
reason: If the strobe becomes flooded, gas build-up can cause the battery cap to forcefully eject off of the strobe or cause the front section of the strobe to violently separate from the back section. Pieces of the strobe can strike the user or others in the vicinity.
distribution: Scuba dive centers and photography stores nationwide sold these strobes, from February 1988 through March 1999, for between $500 and $800.
hazards: If the strobe becomes flooded, gas build-up can cause the battery cap to forcefully eject off of the strobe or cause the front section of the strobe to violently separate from the back section. Pieces of the strobe can strike the user or others in the vicinity.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these strobes. Any strobe suspected of being flooded, which is indicated when the unit either stops working or is corroded, should be returned to an authorized repair center for repair. Sea & Sea is offering a free replacement battery cap with a vent that prevents the gas build up within the strobe.
injuries: CPSC and Sea & Sea have received two reports of injury resulting from the strobes. The first incident, in the Caribbean, occurred when a repair technician had a tooth chipped as he was removing the battery cap. The second incident, in Japan, caused facial lacerations to a consumer when the strobe unit violently broke apart.

title: CPSC & Dynacraft Industries Recall Mountain Bikes
reason: These bikes could have defective handlebar stems, which will not tighten sufficiently to lock onto the bicycles. This can cause the front wheel not to turn properly, resulting in serious injuries to the rider, from falls.
firm: Dynacraft Industries Inc., of San Rafael, Calif.
distribution: Fred Meyer Stores in Alaska, Arizona, Idaho, Oregon, Utah and Washington sold these bikes, from December 1998 through August 18, 1999, for about $160.
hazards: These bikes could have defective handlebar stems, which will not tighten sufficiently to lock onto the bicycles. This can cause the front wheel not to turn properly, resulting in serious injuries to the rider, from falls.
remedies: Consumers should stop riding these bikes immediately and take them to the Fred Meyer Store where purchased, for a free inspection and repair, if needed.
injuries: Dynacraft Industries is not aware of any injuries or incidents involving these bicycles. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: Century Offers Cash Reward for Recalled Infant Swings Four strangulation deaths reported
reason: The swings, which were manufactured by Century from 1991 through 1997, have shoulder harness straps that are placed over each shoulder and buckled between the infant's legs. If the straps on these swings loosen or are unbuckled, an infant can become tangled in the straps and strangle.
firm: Century Products Co., of Macedonia, Ohio
hazards: The swings, which were manufactured by Century from 1991 through 1997, have shoulder harness straps that are placed over each shoulder and buckled between the infant's legs. If the straps on these swings loosen or are unbuckled, an infant can become tangled in the straps and strangle.
remedies: The repair program is no longer available. Parents and caregivers should immediately stop using these infant swings and discard or destroy the product. If you have one of these swings, however, Century is still offering the $30 cash reward to compensate for having to discard or destroy the product.
injuries: These swings were recalled in 1997 following reports of three deaths and one near strangulation from entanglement in the swings' shoulder harness straps. CPSC and Century have since become aware of a fourth death to an 8-month old infant girl in Texas.

title: CPSC, Perfecto Manufacturing Inc. Announce Recall of Aquarium Lights
reason: Sharp edges on these lights could cut the insulation on the wiring. If the wires become exposed, consumers could suffer shocks or electrocution. There is also a risk of fire. In addition, some of these lights could overheat and cause the same problems.
firm: Perfecto Manufacturing Inc., of Noblesville, Ind.
distribution: Pet stores nationwide sold these lights, from August 1998 through July 1999, for a suggested retail price of between $125 and $175.
hazards: Sharp edges on these lights could cut the insulation on the wiring. If the wires become exposed, consumers could suffer shocks or electrocution. There is also a risk of fire. In addition, some of these lights could overheat and cause the same problems.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these aquarium lights, unplug them, and return them to Perfecto for a free replacement.
injuries: CPSC and Perfecto are not aware of any incidents involving these aquarium lights. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Fluke Corp. Announce Second Recall of Electrical Testers
product: Model T-2 hand-held electrical voltage and continuity testers
reason: The batteries in the tester could fail to maintain proper contact due to corrosion within the battery compartment, causing the device to lose power. Consumers testing electrical sources could fail to be warned of the presence of live current if the tester is not powered, posing a risk of shock, electrocution, and thermal burns.
distribution: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial distributors nationwide sold these testers, between December 1997 and September 1999, for about $45.
hazards: The batteries in the tester could fail to maintain proper contact due to corrosion within the battery compartment, causing the device to lose power. Consumers testing electrical sources could fail to be warned of the presence of live current if the tester is not powered, posing a risk of shock, electrocution, and thermal burns.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these voltage and continuity testers immediately, and contact Fluke to obtain a free repair kit or arrange to send your unit to Fluke for repair.
injuries: Fluke is aware of two incidents involving these testers where consumers received a mild electric shock.

title: CPSC, Woods Industries, Inc. Recall Extension Cord Reels
reason: The housing of the extension cord reels could become energized, resulting in electrical shock or electrocution.
firm: Woods Industries, Inc., of Carmel, Ind.
distribution: The cord reels were sold at Lowe's Home Improvement Warehouse stores nationwide, from July 1999 through September 1999, for about $35.
hazards: The housing of the extension cord reels could become energized, resulting in electrical shock or electrocution.
remedies: Unplug the cord reels immediately and stop using them. Woods Industries is offering consumers either a refund or a free replacement extension cord reel. To get a refund, consumers should return their reels to any Lowe's Home Improvement Warehouse.

title: CPSC, Fairlong International Recall Extension Cords
reason: The cords have undersized wires, incorrect ratings, lack overcurrent protection and allow polarize plugs to be incorrectly inserted into the receptacles. These cords present fire, shock and electrocution hazards to consumers.
distribution: Wholesale and discount stores in the Chicago area, and a few stores in Indiana, Iowa, Michigan and Ohio, sold the cords, from July 1997 through October 1999, for about $1 to $2.
hazards: The cords have undersized wires, incorrect ratings, lack overcurrent protection and allow polarize plugs to be incorrectly inserted into the receptacles. These cords present fire, shock and electrocution hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled cords immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund. Consumers also can return the cords directly to the company, for a refund, plus the cost of postage.

title: CPSC & Penda New York Recall Cigarette Lighters
reason: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
distribution: Small stores and souvenir shops in the New York and Miami areas sold the lighters, from January 1999 through July 1999, for about $5.
hazards: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
remedies: Stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund.

title: CPSC & Montgomery Wards Recall Boys Jackets and Sweatshirts
product: North West Blue boys hooded jackets and sweatshirts
reason: The jackets and sweatshirts have hood drawstrings. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that catch on playground equipment, fences or tree branches.
distribution: Montgomery Ward stores nationwide sold the garments, from August 1999 to October 1999, for about $20.
hazards: The jackets and sweatshirts have hood drawstrings. Children can get entangled and strangle in the drawstrings that catch on playground equipment, fences or tree branches.
remedies: Stop wearing the jackets and sweatshirts. Either remove the drawstrings from the hood or discard or destroy these products.

title: CPSC, Holmes Products Corp. Announce Recall of Portable Heaters
reason: The thermostats in some of these heaters are improperly positioned, which can cause them to overheat, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Mass merchandise stores, such as Kmart and Target, sold these heaters, from September 1998 through July 1999, for about $27.
hazards: The thermostats in some of these heaters are improperly positioned, which can cause them to overheat, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these heaters, and contact Holmes for information on how to receive a refund.
injuries: Holmes Products has received 11 reports of these units overheating and catching fire. Six of these incidents resulted in minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC & Stihl Recall Various Weed Trimmers, Brushcutters and Augers
product: Stihl Weed Trimmers, Brushcutters and Augers
reason: Fuel could leak from an unsealed seam in the fuel tank, posing a fire hazard.
firm: Stihl Inc., of Virginia Beach, Va.
distribution: Stihl dealers sold these trimmers, brushcutters and augers, from November 1998 through September 1999, for between $400 and $700, depending on the model purchased.
hazards: Fuel could leak from an unsealed seam in the fuel tank, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Stop using these products immediately, and call Stihl to determine if your trimmer, brushcutter or auger is part of this recall. If so, consumers should return it to an authorized Stihl dealer for a free replacement fuel tank.
injuries: Stihl is aware of one incident in Europe, of a fuel leak from a trimmer. No injuries were reported.

title: CPSC & Midland Consumer Radio Recall Weather Radios
reason: The radio contains a programming error, which can cause the device to fail to recognize certain signals broadcast by the National Weather Service. Consumers could fail to receive some National Weather Service notices advising of a severe weather threat putting lives and property at risk.
firm: Midland Consumer Radio Inc., of Kansas City, Mo.
distribution: Electronic, hardware, mass merchandise stores and truck stops nationwide sold the radios, from May 1999 through August 1999, for about $70.
hazards: The radio contains a programming error, which can cause the device to fail to recognize certain signals broadcast by the National Weather Service. Consumers could fail to receive some National Weather Service notices advising of a severe weather threat putting lives and property at risk.
remedies: Consumers should immediately return the recalled radio to the store where purchased, to receive a new model 74-200 radio that has been programmed correctly. Consumers also can return the radio directly to Midland Consumer Radio, 1670 North Topping Ave., Kansas City, MO 64120 for replacement.

title: CPSC, GE Announce Recall of Dishwashers
reason: The dishwashers have a slide switch that allows consumers to choose between heat drying and energy saver functions. Over time, the slide switch can melt and ignite, presenting a fire hazard.
firm: General Electric (GE) Appliances, of Louisville, Ky.
hazards: The dishwashers have a slide switch that allows consumers to choose between heat drying and energy saver functions. Over time, the slide switch can melt and ignite, presenting a fire hazard.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the recalled dishwashers immediately. Keep the dishwasher door unlatched to prevent the flow of electric current from the latch to the slide switch. GE is offering consumers a rebate toward the purchase of a new dishwasher.
injuries: GE and CPSC have reports of 50 fires, seven of which spread beyond the dishwashers. In three cases, the structure of the house or apartment was damaged. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Shine International Trading Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Cigarette Lighters
reason: The lighters child-resistant mechanisms fail to meet the requirements of the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards. Additionally, the lighters can leak fuel and remain on after consumers have used them, which also presents fire and burn hazards.
distribution: Small stores and souvenir shops nationwide sold these lighters, from August 1998 through July 1999, for about $1.
hazards: The lighters child-resistant mechanisms fail to meet the requirements of the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards. Additionally, the lighters can leak fuel and remain on after consumers have used them, which also presents fire and burn hazards.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Shine International Trading Co. Inc. have received three incident reports with these lighters. One incident involved two lighters that continued to burn after the consumer put them down, one involved two lighters that spontaneously blew apart while unattended, and one involved a lighter that burst into flames resulting in minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, York International Corp. Announce Recall of York International Corporation Diamond 80 Furnaces
product: York International Corporation Diamond 80 downflow mid-efficiency furnaces
reason: Because of inadequate gluing, the insulation surrounding the heat exchanger can separate from the cabinet wall of the furnace, and fall onto the heat exchanger. This could cause surrounding combustible material and drywall to catch on fire, which has the potential to cause burn injuries and deaths.
firm: York International Corp., of York, Pa.
distribution: York dealers sold these furnaces nationwide, from May 1994 through July 1996, for about $680.
hazards: Because of inadequate gluing, the insulation surrounding the heat exchanger can separate from the cabinet wall of the furnace, and fall onto the heat exchanger. This could cause surrounding combustible material and drywall to catch on fire, which has the potential to cause burn injuries and deaths.
remedies: Consumers should contact their local York dealer immediately to schedule a free repair visit.
injuries: York International and CPSC are aware of 11 incidents involving this furnace, including five fires causing $74,000 in property damage.

reason: The candles can burn with a high flame, presenting fire and burn hazards to consumers.

hazards: The candles can burn with a high flame, presenting fire and burn hazards to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the candles immediately, and return the candles to any Bath & Body Works store for a full refund and a $10 gift certificate per customer.

hazards: Small pieces of these foam rubber cows can tear away, posing a serious choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should either throw these cows away immediately or take them to any Gateway Country store location in exchange for another Gateway-brand item of comparable value.
injuries: Gateway has received three reports, by consumers in the U.S., of small pieces of these cows tearing away. There have been no reports of any injuries.

title: CPSC, Benckiser Announce Recall of Scrub Free Daily Shower Cleaner and Daily Shower Spray
product: Scrub Free Daily Shower Cleaner and Scrub Free Daily Shower Spray
reason: The bottles can contain a bacteria. The bacteria usually does not affect healthy individuals, but could cause respiratory or other infections in individuals with chronic health problems or in individuals who have impaired immune systems.
firm: Benckiser Consumer Products Inc. of Greenwich, Conn.
distribution: Supermarket, drug and discount department stores nationwide sold the affected lots of Scrub Free Daily Shower Cleaner and Scrub Free Daily Shower Spray, from May 1999 through October 4, 1999, for about $2 to $4.
hazards: The bottles can contain a bacteria. The bacteria usually does not affect healthy individuals, but could cause respiratory or other infections in individuals with chronic health problems or in individuals who have impaired immune systems.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using Scrub Free Daily Shower Cleaner and Scrub Free Daily Shower Spray purchased prior to October 5, 1999. Shower enclosures that have been sprayed with these products should be washed with a diluted solution of vinegar (one part vinegar to two parts water).
injuries: Benckiser has not received any report of injury associated with this bacteria and these products.
